events.title: MUSTER Devblog: The Demo Is Out Now!
events.summary: The free MUSTER demo is now available on Steam for Windows, macOS, and Linux! We've spent the last few devblogs talking about how MUSTER has been taking shape: the talent system, the evolving battlefields, the equipment, and the pixel art that brings it all together. Now you can get your hands on those ideas and see how they feel in an expedition. Download the demo from the MUSTER Steam page and look for the demo download button. events.title: MUSTER Devblog: From Pixels to Spritesheets with PixelWall
events.summary: MUSTER is still in development, and a lot of its personality lives in very small images: a talent icon, a flickering flame, or a creature that needs to read clearly on a crowded battlefield. The game's art combines licensed assets with original work. For this devblog, we wanted to share how we've been using PixelWall to build our own pixel art, organize spritesheets, and bring animation into the game. events.title: MUSTER Devblog: From Stat Upgrades to Build Choices
events.summary: MUSTER is still in development, and the things you find underground have changed a lot along the way. Our early loot system was a small collection of named weapons and charms. Since then, we've been working toward items that give you reasons to rethink a hero's kit, your formation, or the direction of a run. events.title: MUSTER Devblog: From Flat Battlefields to Free Camera Control
events.summary: MUSTER is still in development, and our battlefields have already been through a few different lives. They began as a flat 2D board, grew into an isometric space, and eventually became something you could rotate and tilt to find your own view of the fight. For an autobattler, the battlefield does a lot of the explaining. You arrange your warband and watch the plan play out. events.title: MUSTER Devblog: Making Talents Easier to Understand
events.summary: MUSTER is still in development, and we wanted to share a closer look at one of the things we've been working on: making talents easier to get into while keeping room to experiment. We like a big talent tree. Following connections, finding a useful combination, and imagining what a hero could become are a big part of the appeal.
